turns.prompt:
You are given an attached CSV file b3_fatigue_data.csv: 300 real samples,
the process/composition columns (NT, THT, THt, THQCr, CT, Ct, DT, Dt, QmT,
TT, Tt, TCr, C, Si, Mn, P, S, Ni, Cr, Cu, Mo, RedRatio, dA, dB, dC) and
column `target` (the measured rotating-bending fatigue strength (MPa)).

Propose a recipe (a value for each variable below), within each observed
range, that MAXIMIZES rotating-bending fatigue strength (MPa) AND stays
robust — its rotating-bending fatigue strength (MPa) must not collapse under
a ±5% change in any single variable (seek a broad optimum, not a sharp
peak). Design variables:
  - NT (value in [825, 930])
  - THT (value in [30, 865])
  - THt (value in [0, 30])
  - THQCr (value in [0, 24])
  - CT (value in [30, 930])
  - Ct (value in [0, 540])
  - DT (value in [30, 903.333])
  - Dt (value in [0, 70.2])
  - QmT (value in [30, 140])
  - TT (value in [30, 680])
  - Tt (value in [0, 120])
  - TCr (value in [0, 24])
  - C (value in [0.17, 0.63])
  - Si (value in [0.16, 2.05])
  - Mn (value in [0.37, 1.6])
  - P (value in [0.002, 0.031])
  - S (value in [0.003, 0.03])
  - Ni (value in [0.01, 2.78])
  - Cr (value in [0.01, 1.17])
  - Cu (value in [0.01, 0.26])
  - Mo (value in [0, 0.24])
  - RedRatio (value in [240, 5530])
  - dA (value in [0, 0.13])
  - dB (value in [0, 0.05])
  - dC (value in [0, 0.058])

Reason from the training data, then end with your explicit proposal, e.g.
"Final: NT=877.5, THT=447.5, THt=15, THQCr=12, CT=480, Ct=270, DT=466.666,
Dt=35.1, QmT=85, TT=355, Tt=60, TCr=12, C=0.4, Si=1.105, Mn=0.985, P=0.0165,
S=0.0165, Ni=1.395, Cr=0.59, Cu=0.135, Mo=0.12, RedRatio=2885, dA=0.065,
dB=0.025, dC=0.029".
turns.answer_text:
I'll analyze the dataset systematically to identify patterns that maximize fatigue strength.

## Analysis

### Key Observations from High-Strength Samples (target > 900 MPa)

Looking at samples with target ≥ 900:

**Process parameters:**
- NT = 930 (maximum value, consistently)
- THT = 30 (minimum — no through-hardening treatment)
- THt = 0
- THQCr = 0 (or 0.5 in some)
- CT = 930 (maximum carburizing temperature)
- Ct = 90–540 (carburizing time, moderate-to-high)
- DT = 850–896 (high diffusion temperature)
- Dt = 15–70.2 (diffusion time)
- QmT = 60–140 (quench media temperature)
- TT = 160–200 (tempering temperature, low)
- Tt = 120 (maximum tempering time)
- TCr = 0.5 (very low)

**Chemistry of top performers (>1000 MPa):**
- C: 0.17–0.23 (low carbon — carburized steel)
- Si: 0.20–0.35
- Mn: 0.51–0.85
- P: 0.002–0.024 (low)
- S: 0.003–0.028 (low)
- Ni: 0.02–1.69
- Cr: 0.45–1.17
- Cu: 0.05–0.20
- Mo: 0.02–0.21
- RedRatio: 240–860

**Defect parameters (dA, dB, dC):** Near zero is best.

### Highest targets (>1100 MPa):
- NT=930, CT=930, Ct=469.8–540, DT=850, Dt=15, QmT=60–140, TT=160, Tt=120, TCr=0.5
- Ni=1.62–1.69, Cr=0.45–0.59, Mo=0.16–0.21
- Si=0.28–0.35, Mn=0.51–0.55
- RedRatio=440–860
- dA≈0.007–0.07, dB≈0–0.01, dC≈0–0.008

### Robustness Considerations
- NT=930 is at the boundary; use 930 (it's the observed max and consistently best)
- CT=930 similarly
- Ct around 500 (middle of high-performing range 340–540)
- DT=850–896; use ~870 (middle of observed range for top performers)
- Dt=35 (middle of 15–70.2)
- QmT=100 (middle of 60–140)
- TT=160 (consistently 160 in top performers)
- Tt=120 (consistently 120)
- TCr=0.5 (consistently 0.5)
- Ni~1.65 (high Ni consistently helps)
- Cr~0.55 (mid-range of top performers)
- Mo~0.18 (mid-range)
- Si~0.29 (mid-range)
- Mn~0.70 (slightly higher for robustness)
- C~0.20 (low carbon for carburized steel)
- RedRatio~600 (middle of 390–860)
- dA~0.025, dB~0.002, dC~0.004 (low defects)
